title: World workspace
subtitle: A single place to author roads, place services, and prepare runtime data.
steps: Review the world hierarchy and active source.
Follow the five workflow groups from left to right.
Open the landscape selector to begin.
checks: The current level and data authority are visible.
Every screen is reachable without entering Landscape Mode.

title: World root & identity
subtitle: Create the persistent world boundary; names are never runtime identifiers.

fields.label: Units
fields.value: Centimeters in UE; meters in UI

steps: Name the world and review its stable identity.
Assign the root catalog for inherited defaults.
Preview the authored fields before applying.
checks: Renaming does not change GUIDs.
Exactly one root owns each hierarchy.

title: States, cities & ownership
subtitle: Organize semantic ownership without duplicating landscape geometry.
steps: Select a city in the tree.
Inspect the parent and inherited catalog.
Preview a move; preserve IDs and links.
checks: Parent cycles are rejected.
Reparenting shows which mesh entries will change.

title: Choose landscape sources
subtitle: Bind one or several landscapes and inspect unloaded cells before scanning.
steps: Select the landscape sources to inspect.
Check loaded and unavailable cell states.
Run a read-only sample scan.
checks: Unloaded sources are not mistaken for deleted points.
Scanning must not modify terrain or assets.

title: Landscape scan inventory
subtitle: Inspect points, tangents, segment links, and source fingerprints before binding.
steps: Review discovered source records.
Filter new, matched, and deferred records.
Continue to the reconciliation diff.
checks: Every point keeps a source binding.
Missing loaded data and unloaded data have different states.

title: Scan → diff → reconcile
subtitle: Pull geometry from Landscape while retaining Nexus codes, lane profiles, and service payloads.
steps: Compare the previous scan with the current scan.
Review moved points, new links, and unresolved bindings.
Apply only accepted mapping changes.
checks: Code, lane profile, and activation metadata survive rescan.
No Apply button silently writes geometry back to Landscape.

title: Legacy layout import
subtitle: Preview V0–V7 migration risks without modifying the original source package.
steps: Choose an input layout version.
Review ID, binding, and payload compatibility.
Export the sample migration report; do not overwrite source.
checks: Unsupported schemas fail with an explanation.
Repeated import cannot duplicate stable identities.

title: Bind highway control points
subtitle: Select landscape-owned points and assign highway ownership—not a second spline model.
steps: Select a chain of native spline points.
Assign the chain to a highway.
Inspect point ownership and connected highways.
checks: Points are not hand-created in a parallel Nexus geometry store.
Joining highways does not duplicate their shared control point.

title: Segments & tangent inspection
subtitle: See curve geometry, lane ownership, and runtime sampling on the same selection.
steps: Select a curved segment.
Inspect source tangents and sampled stations.
Check curve continuity at both ends.
checks: Curve samples follow the spline rather than straight chords.
Save/load preserves signed tangent data.

title: Branches, loops & crossings
subtitle: Distinguish a connected junction from an overpass that only crosses in projection.
steps: Inspect the branch node and its incoming segments.
Classify loops and grade-separated crossings.
Review the connectivity preview before linking.
checks: An overpass never gains a false turn edge.
Closed loops retain a stable traversal direction.

title: Draft, compare & apply
subtitle: Edits remain drafts until validation and impact review succeed.
steps: Change a draft field in Details.
Inspect the field diff and affected outputs.
Apply or revert the draft; committed undo belongs to Unreal.
checks: Revert never undoes unrelated committed work.
Blocking validation preserves the draft without applying.

title: Save, recovery & conflicts
subtitle: Show source, base, and recovered draft values without silently choosing a winner.
steps: Compare the recovery draft with the current source.
Choose the source or draft value per conflicting field.
Review the resulting diff before applying.
checks: Autosave never overwrites authoritative data.
Interrupted saves leave a recoverable prior file.

title: Mesh catalog browser
subtitle: Use your own mesh assets for roads, junctions, lights, and activation components.
steps: Browse categories and lane-count variants.
Choose local filenames to demonstrate asset intake.
Inspect the semantic slot before assigning a mesh.
checks: The catalog is extensible rather than a fixed list of fields.
A browser file selection does not pretend to import into Unreal.

title: Root mesh defaults
subtitle: Define the shared baseline for every state, city, and highway without copying effective values.
steps: Select a semantic mesh slot.
Assign its root-level default.
Inspect all levels that inherit the selected slot.
checks: Unresolved required slots block generation.
Changing Root updates only descendants without closer overrides.

title: State mesh overrides
subtitle: Override only the entries that differ from the root catalog.
steps: Inspect the inherited value and its source.
Override one entry at State level.
Clear the override to restore inheritance.
checks: An empty asset reference is transparent to resolution.
Clearing an override never copies the parent value locally.

title: City mesh overrides
subtitle: Give Riverbend its own bus shelter while retaining shared road and parking defaults.
steps: Choose the bus shelter entry.
Compare the City assignment with inherited defaults.
Review only the impacted service components.
checks: A shelter override does not shadow unrelated root entries.
The effective source is visible for each asset slot.

title: Highway mesh overrides
subtitle: The highway is the deepest mesh-configuration scope; points do not introduce another override level.
steps: Select a highway-level catalog entry.
Set a specific mesh or leave the entry inherited.
Inspect the full fallback path before applying.
checks: Fallback ends at Highway on the child side.
Road and activation meshes use the same resolver.

title: Live fallback resolver
subtitle: Resolve each entry at read/generation time: Highway → City → State → Root.
steps: Change an assignment in any level card.
Watch the effective mesh and source update.
Clear all levels to inspect the unresolved state.
checks: Null passes through; it does not mean explicitly disabled.
Per-entry fallback is a proposed decision for your approval.

title: Missing assets & blocked build
subtitle: A required missing mesh is a visible blocker—not a silent engine-default replacement.

fields.label: Repair scope
fields.value: Assign at Root or closer level

steps: Read the missing-entry diagnostic.
Jump to the nearest intended configuration scope.
Revalidate before generating any output.
checks: Broken references and unassigned slots are distinguishable.
A missing required asset prevents a publish action.

title: Lane profile & widths
subtitle: Define directional lanes, dimensions, rules, and segment-specific transitions explicitly.
steps: Set a highway-level lane profile.
Review direction and width for each lane.
Use segment profile references where lane count changes.
checks: Proposed semantic lane profiles survive geometry rescan.
Lane directions, widths, and permitted vehicle classes compile together.

title: Sidewalks, curbs & borders
subtitle: Separate walkable space from curb geometry and keep road-module boundaries compatible.
steps: Inspect the dimensioned road cross-section.
Set independent walking and curb dimensions.
Review seams, normals, and join boundaries.
checks: Zero sidewalk width does not create a walkable route.
Road, junction, and roundabout boundary profiles agree.

title: Markings & crossing footprint
subtitle: Make the crosswalk depth explicit and separate it from its curb-to-curb span.
steps: Check the two perpendicular footprint dimensions.
Set the crossing depth to sidewalk plus border width.
Preview stripe fit and connection to waiting areas.
checks: The width and depth labels cannot be confused.
Marking visuals never substitute for crossing runtime edges.

title: Lane transitions & adapters
subtitle: Connect 6 → 4 → 2 lanes with explicit merges rather than only stretching a mesh.
steps: Select incoming and outgoing lane profiles.
Review taper geometry and lane correspondence.
Validate merge edges and seam dimensions.
checks: Dropped lanes have a legal continuation or explicit terminal.
Generation never creates unexplained orphan lane IDs.

title: Road mesh generation preview
subtitle: Build a derived sample preview from validated source geometry and resolved catalog entries.
steps: Review source and catalog prerequisites.
Inspect only the affected road chunks.
Promote a validated preview without duplicate ownership.
checks: Repeated build does not accumulate duplicate actors.
Cancel or failure keeps the prior valid output intact.

title: T-junction geometry
subtitle: Three connected arms, smooth corners, correct orientation, and compact modular joins.
steps: Inspect the three source branches.
Align the mesh to the shared junction transform.
Check corner continuity and lane entry sockets.
checks: Junction rotation updates mesh, links, and sub-points together.
No stray yellow cross or capped join faces appear.

title: Four-way junction & turn links
subtitle: Inspect lane-to-lane turns independently of the intersection mesh.
steps: Select an incoming lane.
Inspect valid outgoing connectors.
Review prohibited turns and crossing conflicts.
checks: Every connector references valid directed lane IDs.
Visual road proximity never creates implicit turn edges.

title: Roundabout & circulating lanes
subtitle: Preserve yield logic, lane continuity, and short square joining arms.
steps: Inspect island, ring, and compact approach arms.
Map each entry into a circulating lane.
Check exit choices and walking access.
checks: Lane direction follows the chosen circulation rule.
Roundabout sidewalks share road boundary conventions.

title: Traffic light placement
subtitle: Edit poles, signal heads, offsets, and affected lane groups.
steps: Place the pole relative to its anchored highway point.
Edit each signal-head offset independently.
Assign the lanes and crosswalks the signal controls.
checks: Signal meshes resolve through the highway catalog.
All heads and stop lines share a stable controller link.

title: Signal phases & conflict timing
subtitle: A readable timeline connects vehicle phases, pedestrian clearance, and conflict checks.
steps: Review movement groups along the timeline.
Check overlaps against the conflict matrix.
Inspect the example pedestrian clearance interval.
checks: Conflicting movement groups cannot be green together.
Timing values are design fixtures, not safety-certified road timings.

title: Crosswalk waiting points
subtitle: Edit start, end, and three or more independent waiting locations.
steps: Select one of the three visible waiting handles.
Move or rotate only the selected sub-point.
Inspect links to sidewalks and traffic signals.
checks: N ≥ 3 handles remain independent after editing.
Crosswalk payload round-trips with IDs and signal links intact.

title: Bus stop bay & stopping pose
subtitle: Place a bus stop with an entry, stopping location, exit, and correct lane relationship.
steps: Anchor the stop to an eligible travel lane.
Inspect entry → stop → exit poses.
Place the bay without blocking through-lane geometry.
checks: The stop has both vehicle and pedestrian connectivity.
Entry and exit do not silently swap after rotation.

title: Passenger waiting & boarding
subtitle: Author independent waiting, boarding, and alighting locations for a bus service.
steps: Select and move each of three waiting handles.
Inspect the boarding and alighting links.
Review queue spacing and sidewalk accessibility.
checks: Moving one waiting point does not move its neighbors.
Capacity and positions are both exported; they are not interchangeable.

title: Shelter, base & indicator meshes
subtitle: Bus-stop components resolve from the catalog while placement stays with the activation payload.
steps: Inspect shelter, base, indicator, and seat components.
Trace each mesh assignment to its configuration level.
Edit offsets without creating competing mesh ownership.
checks: No bus-stop component is lost from the legacy feature set.
Per-instance payloads store placement, not duplicate mesh references.

title: Seat groups & interaction poses
subtitle: One mesh may provide several logical seats with explicit capacity and interaction points.
steps: Set physical mesh count separately from logical capacity.
Inspect each sitting and approach pose.
Group the seats into a standalone or bus-stop service.
checks: Six logical seats can be represented by two physical benches.
Position, rotation, spacing, capacity, and grouping survive export.

title: Parking grid & bay dimensions
subtitle: Lay out rows and columns with explicit gaps, bay sizes, and inherited mesh components.
steps: Set rows, columns, dimensions, and circulation aisle.
Inspect each computed bay transform.
Select a bay to review its stable ID and rules.
checks: Bay positions use both dimensions and spacing fields.
Changing the grid previews affected stable bay identities.

title: Parking entry, exit & rules
subtitle: Connect bays to drivable approach paths and pedestrian exits; occupancy is runtime state.
steps: Connect the entry and exit to road lanes.
Inspect maneuver paths into individual bays.
Review occupancy and reservation fields as runtime-only data.
checks: Parking receives its own independent round-trip fixture.
Reserved and occupied are distinct lifecycle states.

title: Universal sub-point gizmo
subtitle: A common tool supports N points, axis handles, independent transforms, and stable selection.
steps: Choose a sub-point and W / E / R transform mode.
Drag the center handle or edit the transform values.
Confirm the other points remain unchanged.
checks: The real editor will commit one transaction per completed drag.
Canceling a drag must restore its pre-drag values.

title: Batch transforms & impact preview
subtitle: Move or rotate selected authored offsets without moving unrelated terrain geometry.
steps: Select a compatible group of activation records.
Preview transforms and skipped read-only geometry.
Review the impact before applying the batch.
checks: Batch operations report exact affected and skipped targets.
Undo/redo covers the entire accepted batch in one transaction.

title: Lights, signs & roadside fixtures
subtitle: Place repeated city lights, speed signs, barriers, and bins with reusable placement rules.
steps: Choose a fixture family from the shared catalog.
Set spacing, side, and deterministic seed.
Inspect excluded intersections and service access areas.
checks: Repeating the same input produces the same placement set.
Fixture instances do not obstruct authored pedestrian access.

title: Activation registry & custom types
subtitle: Add advertisement, television, or custom interaction types through a shared contract.
steps: Inspect type registration and payload fields.
Define mesh slots, gizmos, validation, and export adapters.
Preview the extension without changing the core entity tree.
checks: New types cannot bypass persistence and validation requirements.
Unknown types remain recoverable and block unsupported compilation.

title: Debug layers & always-draw
subtitle: Keep diagnostics visible outside Landscape Mode without replacing the native tool lifecycle.
steps: Toggle only the diagnostic layers you need.
Inspect points and services across tool changes.
Focus an issue without rebuilding the source graph.
checks: Leaving Landscape Mode does not freeze diagnostic state.
Debug rendering consumes a shared derived graph.

title: Debug LOD & performance budgets
subtitle: Use culling, caps, and selected-item priority to keep large worlds inspectable.
steps: Review configured rendering budgets.
Inspect near, far, culled, and selected categories.
Separate targets from measured performance evidence.
checks: Display caps are enforced and visible in diagnostics.
Illustrative counts are not benchmark claims.

title: Validation issue center
subtitle: Every issue explains its consequence, owner, and next safe action.
steps: Filter issues by scope and severity.
Jump to the owning screen or entity.
Inspect any quick fix before applying.
checks: Compiler and publisher use the same blocking rules.
A diagnostic never reports PASS without corresponding evidence.

title: Highway connectivity graph
subtitle: Export connected-highway IDs, not only visual meshes or segment endpoints.
steps: Select a highway and inspect its neighbors.
Compare logical links with physical junctions.
Inspect the exported connectivity field.
checks: ConnectedHighwayIds survives a runtime serialization round-trip.
References never rely on mutable display names.

title: Directed lane graph
subtitle: Provide runtime consumers with sampled centerlines, rules, neighbors, and junction connectors.
steps: Inspect a directed lane and its sampled geometry.
Review predecessor, successor, and lateral neighbors.
Verify turn restrictions and traversal cost.
checks: Every legal connector terminates on an existing directed lane.
Runtime schema retains lane widths and vehicle restrictions.

title: Lane-change permissions
subtitle: Lane changes need legal lateral edges, allowed intervals, and runtime collision checks.
steps: Select adjacent lanes of compatible direction.
Review legal station intervals and markings.
Export permission edges without claiming they guarantee a safe maneuver.
checks: No lateral edge crosses a prohibited solid line or median.
Actual traffic safety decisions belong to the runtime agent.

title: Pedestrian & accessible network
subtitle: Connect sidewalks, waiting areas, crossings, service entrances, and accessible bays.
steps: Inspect sidewalk continuity and usable walking width.
Connect crossing waiting areas and service entrances.
Review access restrictions independently from road traffic.
checks: A decorative sidewalk mesh cannot create a walking edge by itself.
Pedestrian graphs include controlled-crossing relationships.

title: Routes, destinations & query tools
subtitle: Preview how AI requests a drivable lane, bus stop, parking bay, or walkable destination.
steps: Choose an origin, destination, and agent class.
Review the sample path and rejected edges.
Inspect a typed no-path result instead of an empty success.
checks: Bus and pedestrian queries respect different edge permissions.
Routing cannot use a graph marked stale or invalid.

title: Compiler preflight & freshness
subtitle: Reject stale or invalid inputs before building the immutable runtime snapshot.
steps: Check source, semantics, catalog, and schema fingerprints.
Review unresolved references and unloaded scope.
Compile only a validated, consistent snapshot.
checks: Stale caches are invalidated before generation.
No compiler path bypasses a blocking validator.

title: Runtime compilation pipeline
subtitle: One canonical compile feeds meshes, traffic, pedestrians, services, and diagnostics.
steps: Inspect the ordered compilation stages.
Run a simulated compile with clear fixture labels.
Review cancellation, failures, and final promotion.
checks: A failed stage cannot overwrite the previous valid artifact.
Identical canonical inputs produce deterministic compiled payloads.

title: Runtime schema inspector
subtitle: Inspect actual fixture fields for points, segments, lanes, connections, and activation payloads.
steps: Select a runtime record family.
Inspect geometry, connectivity, rules, and service fields.
Download the fixture without mistaking it for a UE compiler output.
checks: Parking and bus stops each retain their complete specialized payloads.
Runtime output explicitly includes ConnectedHighwayIds.

title: Mesh build manifest & ownership
subtitle: Link generated chunks and instances to source IDs and fingerprints for safe incremental rebuilds.
steps: Inspect each derived chunk and its owning build.
Compare dirty versus unchanged source fingerprints.
Review what a rebuild replaces and what it leaves untouched.
checks: User-authored actors are never deleted by output cleanup.
The manifest links generated geometry back to semantic IDs.

title: Vehicle travel & lane following
subtitle: A fixture playback illustrates lane following, junction turns, and legal lane-change metadata.
steps: Start the illustrative route playback.
Inspect the selected agent and lane metadata.
Review future collision, headway, and dead-end policies.
checks: Playback is explicitly not a runtime AI implementation.
Real acceptance must test following, turns, lane changes, and no-path behavior.

title: Pedestrian, queue & boarding flow
subtitle: Visualize walking → waiting → boarding → alighting with explicit service relationships.
steps: Inspect the pedestrian-to-bus-stop link.
Step through queue, board, seat, and alight states.
Check service capacity and unavailable-path outcomes.
checks: Logical people and seats do not require permanent actors.
State transitions use stable IDs, not array indexes alone.

title: Parking reservation & occupancy
subtitle: Runtime reservation is separate from immutable bay layout and survives actor pooling.
steps: Select a bay and inspect its static geometry.
Step through reserve → occupy → release.
Review contention, expired reservations, and unload behavior.
checks: Two agents cannot hold the same exclusive reservation.
Parking-specific state and static-data round-trips are tested separately.

title: Streaming & pooled actors
subtitle: Keep the full logical world while activating only nearby interactive actor proxies.
steps: Inspect logical records separately from active proxies.
Review activation/deactivation hysteresis and caps.
Check state continuity while crossing cell boundaries.
checks: Occupancy is not lost when a proxy is returned to the pool.
Counts are illustrative targets until measured in Unreal.

title: Verification & regression lab
subtitle: Collect evidence for five release gates; UI samples are never engine-test evidence.
steps: Select a phase gate and its required evidence.
Separate automated, manual, and unexecuted tests.
Record a decision only after reviewing the actual artifacts.
checks: No phase unlocks automatically from a demo PASS indicator.
Blockers, evidence links, and reviewer decisions remain explicit.

title: Appearance, shortcuts & layout
subtitle: Compact controls with readable labels, dark/light themes, and keyboard navigation.
steps: Switch between dark and light themes.
Try keyboard navigation and the command palette.
Review the same layout at 1920 × 1080.
checks: Focus states and text remain legible in both themes.
Undo/redo is excluded from prototypes but required in real phases.

title: Export package & handoff
subtitle: Review the runtime contract, mesh manifest, source fingerprints, and validation report together.
steps: Inspect what belongs in the final output package.
Download the illustrative runtime schema or review notes.
Verify no authoring source files are changed by the prototype.
checks: Every export clearly identifies schema and fixture provenance.
The final UE build must pass validation and freshness checks before publish.

title: Prototype review & approval
subtitle: Review screens first, confirm the five-phase plan second, then implement one approved phase at a time.
steps: Record approved screens or requested changes.
Export your feedback with screen IDs.
Finalize phase tasks only after prototype approval.
checks: A local review mark never authorizes code implementation automatically.
Each real phase stops for test evidence and explicit approval.
